title: Guaranteed logic-level noise margins with ground offset
description: Check high and low recognition margins between a driver and receiver using guaranteed voltage limits, a signed ground offset and adverse line-noise bounds. Negative results identify incompatible corners.
formula: DeltaG = GND_receiver - GND_driver; NMH = VOH_min - DeltaG - VIH_min - noise_high; NML = VIL_max - VOL_max + DeltaG - noise_low; NM = min(NMH,NML)
assumptions: Single-ended positive logic; all driver levels reference driver ground and receiver thresholds reference receiver ground. Positive ground_offset raises receiver ground.

Use worst-case voltage guarantees at the actual supply, temperature and loading. noise_high is an adverse downward voltage disturbance; noise_low is an adverse upward disturbance, both entered as positive magnitudes.

A nonnegative result checks logic recognition only. Separately check input absolute/recommended voltage limits, power-off tolerance, current fanout, edge rates, ringing and timing. Zero margin leaves no extra noise allowance.

references.title: Texas Instruments SZZA036C, section 5 and Figure 50: logic compatibility
Texas Instruments SCAA029, Figure 23: DC noise margin

constraints.message: Driver high guarantee must exceed its low guarantee
Receiver high threshold must exceed its low threshold

title: Logic output DC-current fanout
description: Find the maximum whole number of identical receiver inputs that a logic output can drive in both states, and check current headroom for a proposed load count.
formula: NH = floor(Isource/IIH); NL = floor(Isink/abs(IIL)); Nmax = min(NH,NL); headroom_H = Isource-N*IIH; headroom_L = Isink-N*abs(IIL)
assumptions: Enter all currents as nonnegative magnitudes. In particular, convert negative datasheet IOH and IIL to positive magnitudes; their conventional terminal-current signs are not used in this budget.
Identical loads and worst-case input currents; driver limits must be guaranteed operating currents at the required VOH/VOL, not absolute-maximum current ratings.

This is DC fanout only. Capacitive loading, edge-rate limits, transient switching current, package current limits, voltage compatibility, bus hold and transmission-line behavior can impose a smaller practical load count.
Receiver current magnitudes must be strictly positive; an ideal zero-current receiver does not have a finite current-limited fanout. Zero driver capability and zero proposed loads are valid.

references.title: Texas Instruments SZZA036C, sections 3.3, 4.6.12-4.6.14 and 5: terminal signs, input currents and loading
Texas Instruments SCEA046B, Slow or Noisy Edges: heavily loaded output edge-rate limitation

outputs.label: DC fanout valid in both states

constraints.message: Receiver count must be a whole number

title: CMOS logic internal and output-load power budget
description: Estimate a bank of identical CMOS logic sections using characterized per-section power-dissipation capacitance, separate input/output cycle rates, external loading and whole-package quiescent current.
formula: Pstatic = V*Iq; Pinternal = N*Cpd*V^2*fi; Pload = N*CL*V^2*fo; Ptotal = Pstatic+Pinternal+Pload; Iaverage = Ptotal/V
assumptions: Cpd is the manufacturer's characterized equivalent internal power-dissipation capacitance per active section, not the input pin capacitance. It includes internal node charging and through-current under its stated test conditions.
All active sections share the entered Cpd, external capacitance and cycle rates. Frequencies count full low-high-low cycles per second, equivalently low-to-high charging events, not both edges.
Rail-to-rail, sufficiently fast transitions; Cpd must match the supply, input slew, temperature, enabled state and switching pattern. Whole-package quiescent current is added once.

External loads are capacitive and charge fully. Excludes resistive termination power, intermediate input-level extra ICC, power-off injection, and thermal prediction. Ptotal is supply power, not a universal allocation of heat to the package.

references.title: Texas Instruments SCAA035B, equations 3-10 and Cpd testing considerations

inputs.label: Input cycles per second per section

constraints.message: Active section count must be a whole number

title: Synchronizer metastability reliability budget
description: Estimate single-chain and identical-chain system MTBF logarithmically, and compare available metastability resolution time with a required system reliability target.
formula: MTBFchain = exp(tres/tau)/(T0*fclock*fdata); MTBFsystem = MTBFchain/N; trequired = max(0,tau*ln(MTBFtarget*N*T0*fclock*fdata)); margin = tres-trequired
assumptions: T0 and tau are positive technology-characterized metastability fit parameters in seconds. Numerical defaults are illustrative, not specifications for any part or process.

fdata counts asynchronous transitions, not square-wave periods. The random relative phase and rare-event exponential resolution model must apply; T0*fdata must be less than one and in practice much less than one.

resolution_time is the effective available regeneration time under the same time-origin convention as the fitted T0/tau. Obtain it from characterized cells and routed timing, not merely the nominal clock period.

System estimate assumes N identical independent rare-failure chains; their failure rates add. This does not make separately synchronized bits coherent and does not guarantee pulse capture or correct CDC protocol.

MTBF outputs are log10(MTBF / 1 second), avoiding exponent overflow. No absolute lifetime or certification claim; correlated events, PVT changes and invalid fit extrapolation require a different model.

references.title: Stanford EE183, Ryan Donohue, Synchronization in Digital Logic Circuits: MTBF and synchronizer requirements, pages 1-4

inputs.label: Required system mean time between failures

outputs.label: log10 of single-chain MTBF in seconds
log10 of system MTBF in seconds
Resolution time required for target system MTBF

constraints.message: Synchronizer chain count must be a whole number
The aperture-times-transition-rate factor must be below one; rare-event characterization must also be valid

title: Three-stage CMOS logical-effort gate sizing
description: Size the two internal input capacitances of a fixed unbranched three-gate CMOS path for minimum first-order delay, given its endpoint load and gate logical efforts.
formula: F = g1*g2*g3*CL/C1; f = F^(1/3); C2 = C1*f/g1; C3 = CL*g3/f; D = 3*f+P; tpath = tau*D
assumptions: Exactly three fixed-topology static CMOS gates with no side branches or significant interconnect capacitance. Logical efforts are relative to an equal-drive reference inverter and are at least one in this ordinary static-CMOS model.

Gate input capacitance scales continuously with size; parasitic path delay P is the sum of all three normalized gate parasitics and is assumed independent of size. tau is a characterized process delay unit, not an RC component value.

Equal stage effort minimizes delay in the linear logical-effort model. Actual standard-cell choices, minimum size, asymmetric pin effort, input slew, routing, rise/fall imbalance and PVT require library timing or transistor-level simulation.
The result sizes gates for an already chosen stage count and logic polarity; it does not choose an optimal integer stage count or verify register setup.

references.title: David Harris, Logical Effort, pages 6-9 and 13-16: d=gh+p, equal stage effort and backward sizing

title: Hardware FIFO depth from burst and service guarantees
description: Size usable FIFO word storage and its bit capacity from a bounded burst/sustained arrival envelope and a guaranteed latency-rate read service; also estimate the FIFO delay bound.
formula: alpha(t)=b+r*t; beta(t)=R*max(0,t-T); for R>=r, Bmax=b+r*T; usable_depth=ceil(Bmax); storage_bits=word_bits*usable_depth; delay_bound=T+b/R
assumptions: One initially empty hardware FIFO with fixed-width words and FIFO-ordered service. The arrival bound b+r*t must hold for every time interval, not merely on average.

Read service must guarantee a rate-latency service curve R*max(0,t-T). service_latency includes all bounded arbitration stalls, CDC/empty-flag delay and one word-service interval for asynchronous completion phase.

The entered latency is at least 1/service_rate for this whole-word asynchronous service model. Service rate must be at least the sustained arrival rate; otherwise no finite perpetual-depth guarantee exists.

Calculated depth is a sufficient usable capacity under these envelopes, not necessarily the smallest depth for a known discrete schedule. Add implementation-reserved entries, ECC/metadata and vendor memory granularity separately; no implicit power-of-two rounding.

This sizes storage, not synchronizer reliability, Gray-pointer correctness, metastability containment or absolute interface timing. Unbounded stalls or an invalid arrival/service guarantee invalidate the result.

references.title: Le Boudec and Thiran, Network Calculus, section 1.4.1, Theorems 1.4.1-1.4.2 and Figure 1.10
Stanford EE183, Synchronization in Digital Logic Circuits, pages 5-7: dual-port hardware FIFOs and conservative pointer synchronization

inputs.label: Guaranteed service latency including word phase

constraints.message: Burst allowance must be a whole number of words
Word width must be a whole number of bits
Guaranteed service rate must cover the sustained arrival rate
Whole-word asynchronous service latency must include at least one word-service interval
